added_failures_note: derived from gate-base.log and gate-head.log directly: both arms report 4 passed and no FAILED id, so the run added none; the manifest's own baseline_suite/after_suite values are inline unquoted-key objects the standard reader cannot parse.

durability.reason: a measurement node adds no product test by brief; its controls are the 10-item pilot cost and the recorded exclusion counts, and the module it measures is pinned by tests/standard_names/test_segment_selection.py

findings.text: blocking: the fragment says the family agreement groups "the golden positives", but run.py:333 groups every record with label == 1, the 167 golden positives plus the 174 human-edit targets, so the reported 101 multi-member families is the 341-record figure, not the 15 a golden-positives-only cohort gives.
follow-on: the _DERIVED_RECORD_FIELDS docstring reads "Dropping them keeps the committed results stay under the data-file size the repository allows", which is ungrammatical and names no mechanism.

follow-on: the driver's per-slot accuracy (_slot_accuracy at run.py:307 and the slot_match dict at run.py:261) duplicates exact_match_accuracy, which the repository already owns at benchmark_roles.py:259, instead of importing it.

follow-on: baseline_suite and after_suite are written as inline objects with unquoted keys, which reckon.crew.review._gate_log_path cannot parse, so the run's added-failure count is unmeasurable from its own manifest and had to be derived by reading gate-base.log and gate-head.log directly.
